meta.subtitle: Second-quarter revenue grew 34% with net cash and positive free cash flow, but GAAP losses and founder control temper the case

analystCommentary:
Viant is growing quickly. Second-quarter 2026 revenue rose 34%, and the MD&A describes strengthening advertiser demand across industry verticals, continued demand for connected TV and expanded use of its ViantAI product suite.

At $12.24 on October 2, 2026 the shares sit in the upper half of their 52-week range of $8.11 – $14.80. All 11 covering analysts rate Buy.

The growth is not yet showing up in GAAP profit: the company reported a net loss in the quarter, and gross profit is growing more slowly than revenue (see Financials). We think the balance sheet and cash generation give it room to invest through that, and that the price leaves upside if growth holds. Control by the founding family is the main governance caveat (see Management).

executiveSummary.companyOverview:
Viant Technology Inc. is an advertising technology company. Its cloud-based demand side platform lets marketers and their agencies plan, buy and measure programmatic advertising across connected TV (CTV), streaming audio, digital out-of-home, mobile and desktop.

Its products include the ViantAI suite, Household ID and IRIS_ID. On May 1, 2026 it completed the acquisition of TVision, adding attention measurement and data capabilities.

The company was founded in 1999 and is headquartered in Irvine, California.

thesis.body: Viant is growing revenue at a rate well above FY25's, has no debt, and generates free cash flow. If it sustains growth near consensus and converts more of it into operating profit, the shares should move toward the Street's targets. The scenario math in Valuation supports a BUY.

catalysts: Continued revenue growth in the seasonally strong fourth quarter.
Integration of TVision into Viant's measurement offering.
Adoption of AI Decisioning and the Outcomes performance solution.
A return to GAAP operating profit.
risks: Revenue concentration among agency holding companies.
Gross profit growing more slowly than revenue.
Reduced access to data and advertising inventory.

financials.incomeCommentary:
FY25 revenue was $344.2M, up 19.0%, after growth of 29.7% in FY24. Operating margin turned positive at 1.2% in FY24 and reached 3.5% in FY25, and diluted EPS rose to $0.36 from $0.14.

Growth picked up in 2026. Second-quarter revenue was $104.3 million, up 34%, and first-half revenue rose 30%. The MD&A credits growing customer adoption of newer products and platform features.

The counter-case is profitability. Second-quarter gross profit rose 27% to $45.5 million and contribution ex-TAC rose 24%, both slower than revenue, and the trailing gross margin has slipped to 44.5% from 45.8% in FY25. The company reported a net loss of $(1.8) million in the quarter against net income of $1.8 million a year earlier, and an operating margin of -3.7%. Adjusted EBITDA rose 26% to $14.2 million, so the gap between adjusted and GAAP results is wide.
financials.balanceCommentary:
Viant reports no debt, and trailing net debt to EBITDA is -6.4x, meaning cash exceeds borrowings. The trailing current ratio is 2.34, down from 4.24 in FY21 but still comfortable.

That balance sheet gives the company room to keep investing in growth while GAAP results are negative, which lowers the risk of the current losses. The excerpt does not say how the TVision acquisition was paid for.
financials.cashflowCommentary:
Free cash flow was $34.3M in FY25, a 10.0% FCF margin, and FCF margins have been positive in four of the last five years. Our free cash flow deducts all capital expenditure, which was $18.3M in FY25, so investment in the platform absorbs a meaningful share of operating cash flow. The trailing FCF yield is 5.9%: in our view that supports the balance sheet rather than the valuation, which rests on earnings growth (see Valuation).

The counter-case is the gap to earnings: FY25 free cash flow was well above FY25 net income of $8.4M, and the excerpt does not reconcile the two. Until GAAP profit catches up, we treat the cash flow as supportive but would want to see what drives the gap before relying on it fully.

valuation.multiplesCommentary:
At $12.24 DSP trades at 35.0x trailing earnings, 20.3x NTM earnings, ~15.6x FY27E earnings, 2.1x trailing sales and 20.7x trailing EV/EBITDA.

Consensus expects EPS of $0.60 for FY26E and $0.79 for FY27E, against FY25 diluted EPS of $0.36. The consensus basis is not stated; the company reports non-GAAP net income and Adjusted EBITDA, and with GAAP results negative in 2026 so far, the estimates are most likely on an adjusted basis. The trailing P/E is GAAP, so the two are not directly comparable; we anchor our Base case on the forward multiple, accepting that it may flatter the stock.

The Street is uniformly positive: 11 Buy ratings, with a consensus target of $19.50, a median of $19.00 and a range of $17.00–$24.00.

We have no peer multiples to compare against.

scenarios.name: Bull
scenarios.driver: Revenue keeps growing near the 2026 pace, TVision and ViantAI lift margins, and GAAP profit returns. The shares reach the Street median target.

scenarios.name: Base
scenarios.driver: Viant delivers close to consensus revenue and earnings, with margins improving slowly, and the NTM multiple holds near today's 20.3x as estimates roll forward toward FY27E. The shares rise but stay below the lowest Street target of $17.00.

scenarios.name: Bear
scenarios.driver: An agency holding company cuts spending or ad budgets tighten, revenue growth slows and losses persist. The shares fall back toward the 52-week low.

valuation.scenarioCommentary:
Base carries the most weight because it requires only that Viant delivers the consensus path, which already includes the margin improvement implied by EPS rising faster than revenue, at an unchanged forward multiple. Bull carries more weight than Bear because revenue growth has accelerated and the net cash position cushions a downturn. Bear still carries a quarter of the weight because of the concentration and cyclical risks set out in Risks.

The result is a weighted fair value of $14.35, an expected upside of +17.2% and a bear-case downside of -30.6%. That clears our BUY threshold.

Our $13–$16 target range brackets Base. It sits below the Street's range because we give more weight than the Street to the GAAP losses, the controlled-company structure and low customer switching costs.

segments.name: Consolidated
segments.body: Viant reports a single segment. Revenue comes from platform fees, charged primarily as a percentage of spend under master service agreements or at a fixed price per thousand impressions under insertion orders, plus separate service fees for data management, media execution and advanced reporting.

moatFactors.name: Proprietary data and identity
moatFactors.body: Household ID, IRIS_ID and attention signals, now extended by TVision, give Viant data that customers can use to target and measure campaigns. The 10-Q warns that the effectiveness of the platform would decrease if its access to data were diminished.

moatFactors.name: Switching costs
moatFactors.body: The 10-Q says customers typically have relationships with numerous providers and can use both Viant's platform and competitors' without significant cost or disruption, and that contracts generally carry no long-term or exclusive obligations.

moatFactors.name: Independence
moatFactors.body: The MD&A says engagement with enterprise brands reflects advertiser interest in independent and transparent buy-side alternatives. In our view, that positioning helps win business but is not a barrier competitors cannot also offer.

businessMoat.durability: We rate the moat NARROW. Viant's proprietary data and identity tools give it a real, if modest, advantage, but its own filing says customers can switch between platforms easily and are not bound by long-term contracts. Its position depends on continued product improvement rather than structural protection.

points: Consensus expects FY26E revenue of ~$442.6M, up 29%, and FY27E revenue of $533M. Given first-half growth of 30%, the FY26E figure looks achievable if fourth-quarter seasonality holds.

The MD&A says Viant has benefited, and expects to keep benefiting, from the shift of advertising budgets from linear television to CTV, which represents a growing portion of activity on its platform. In our view, that shift is the main driver of the growth outlook.
AI Decisioning and Outcomes extend ViantAI toward automated campaign planning and execution. Their contribution is not yet quantified in the filing.
Management plans to keep increasing operating expenses to invest in growth, which may delay a return to GAAP profit.

management.leadership: Per the proxy statement dated April 2026, Tim Vanderhook is Chief Executive Officer and Chairman, and Chris Vanderhook is Chief Operating Officer and a director. They founded the company with their brother Russ Vanderhook, Senior Vice President and Co-Founder. Founder-led management gives continuity; the open question for holders is whether the team can turn faster growth into GAAP profit.
management.capitalAllocation: Viant pays no dividend and our data shows no repurchase amounts for FY21 to FY25. Its main capital decision in 2026 was the TVision acquisition, which expands into audience measurement (see Risks). In our view, the net cash position gives management room for further acquisitions, and the test is whether TVision lifts adoption of Viant's measurement products.
management.governance:
Viant is a controlled company. Per the proxy statement dated April 2026, Tim Vanderhook, Chris Vanderhook and Capital V LLC hold more than 50% of the voting power for the election of directors through Class B common stock. The company is therefore exempt from Nasdaq rules requiring a majority-independent board and fully independent compensation and nominating committees, and the proxy says it uses some of these exemptions. The Board has determined that Max Valdes, Brett Wilson and Vivian Yang are independent.

The proxy also discloses an aircraft lease, signed in April 2022, with Capital V, in which the three brothers each hold a one-third interest. The rent was $14,500 per flight hour during the initial term and is subject to adjustment at each annual renewal, so the current rate is not disclosed in the excerpt. For public holders, control plus related-party dealings means fewer formal protections than at a widely held company.
management.insiderOwnership:
As of April 9, 2026, Capital V LLC held 42.86% of total voting power, Tim Vanderhook 13.63% and Chris Vanderhook 13.77%, and all executive officers and directors as a group held 29.43%. Capital V, Tim Vanderhook and Chris Vanderhook together form the Vanderhook Parties that the proxy says hold majority voting control. Punch & Associates Investment Management, Inc. held 6.32% and BlackRock, Inc. 5.65% of the Class A common stock.

For outside holders, this means the founding family decides board elections and other shareholder votes. Its large economic stake gives it reason to grow the value of the company, but minority holders have little influence over strategy or governance.

idiosyncratic: Customer concentration: the 10-Q says Viant receives a significant amount of revenue from a select number of advertising agency holding companies. In our view, this is a central operating risk, since one holding company shifting budgets could slow growth sharply. What to watch: whether revenue growth stays near the 34% second-quarter pace through the fourth quarter.

Data access: the 10-Q warns that the restriction of third-party cookies and the use of automated opt-out signals could cause instability in the advertising technology industry, and separately that diminished access to data would decrease the platform's effectiveness. In our view, Viant's own identity tools partly offset this risk; a further slip in gross margin from the trailing 44.5% would be an early sign that data costs are rising.

Inventory access: the 10-Q says revenue could decline if access to advertising inventory diminishes or fails to grow. In our view, this risk rises if Viant's independence puts it at odds with large media owners; continued growth in CTV activity on the platform is the signal that access is holding.

TVision integration: the 10-Q warns that TVision brings risks relating to panel-based measurement technology, the accuracy and reliability of measurement data, increased competition from established measurement providers, and intellectual property litigation.
risks.systemic: The MD&A says advertising spend is closely tied to advertisers' financial performance, and that a downturn could hurt the digital advertising market and Viant's results. Revenue is also seasonal, with the fourth quarter historically the strongest, and political advertising can swing results across election cycles.

body: BUY, target range $13–$16, based on the scenarios in Valuation.
We would add conviction if gross margin stabilizes and GAAP operating profit returns. We would cut to HOLD if revenue growth slows sharply or if an agency holding company reduces its spending.
